finding: No test feeds check_diagnosis an Outside writes line that is not a list item; the new `not a list item` branch is unpinned.
why: Replacing the message with None survives all tests; refusal of a prose line in Outside writes is never asserted.
fix: Add a test with an Outside writes line without a dash; assert not ok and a problem containing `not a list item`.
evidence: mutant `else "not a list item"` -> `else None`: SURVIVED

finding: Line-end detection uses splitlines(keepends=True), which also breaks on form feed, \x1c-\x1e, \x85, U+2028/2029; an entry ending in such a character gets the new entry glued onto its physical line.
why: append on `- ticket: 12\x0c\n` yields `- ticket: 12\x0c- in-review: 12\x0c\n`: two entries on one physical line.
fix: Split lines on \n only in _read_lines; test a form feed at the end of the last entry.

finding: BOM is a literal invisible U+FEFF inside the quotes, not an escape.
why: A tool that strips zero-width characters turns BOM into an empty string and the BOM logic misbehaves silently.
evidence: od -c shows bytes 357 273 277 between the quotes

criterion: assertion-strength: test does not exercise the behaviour it names
finding: The BOM test puts the BOM before `# Diagnosis`, not a `## ` heading, so the BOM never touches the code under test.
why: Removing the BOM strip in sections() and repeated() both survive.
fix: Put the BOM directly before a `## ` heading and assert ok.
evidence: removeprefix(BOM) removed in sections and repeated: SURVIVED

finding: No test gives a State row whose Read from names only a backticked non-kind word (a typo).
why: Dropping `& kinds` survives; a typoed kind would match nothing instead of failing the format.
fix: Add a _format_with case swapping a kind for an unknown backticked word; expect exit 2.

finding: read_first tests never assert Outcome.attempts; the read-first path's attempts=0 is unpinned.
fix: Assert outcome.attempts == 0 in the find-unlisted-write test.
